sections.title: Candidate construction
paragraphs: The union uses same-page greedy one-to-one matching at normalized title similarity ≥0.90. It strips HTML, normalizes Unicode and alphanumeric text, and uses SequenceMatcher with autojunk=False. Matched source candidates are deduplicated; unmatched candidates are merged while preserving relative order. This operates on parser outputs, not gold labels.

sections.title: Prompt and decoding
paragraphs: The frozen PROMPT asks for logical hierarchy, treats executive summaries/main sections/annexes as top level, rejects captions, table cells, running headers, emphasis and TOC entries, and requires consistent parallel sections. Cover text must not shift body levels; absolute page number must not determine level. The complete prompt is linked in the runner.

The decoder strips a code-fence wrapper, then validates every ID and value. Accepted IDs are joined back to their original titles and pages; null rejects a candidate. A missing source title cannot be created by this method. Invalid responses are recorded as errors and yield no accepted headings for that document.

sections.title: Prompt and memory update
paragraphs: INSTRUCTION asks for genuine headings on the current page, their complete text and levels H1–H6. It excludes running headers/footers, captions, sidebars and TOC entries, treats document instructions as content, and permits recovery of titles missing from the outline. Tags and previous predictions are described as possibly wrong.

The full-document outline contains candidate titles and pages but omits the parser’s levels. Only earlier sampled pages can become image memory; unseen intervening pages are not silently supplied. Native target-page text is extracted in sorted order.

sections.title: Labels and features
paragraphs: A single assistant reviewed source text, layout/page snippets and TOC context and supplied explicit line groups and H levels. The annotation provenance does not record a precise teacher-model checkpoint, and there was no independent human adjudication. These labels are reviewable training targets, not demonstrated 100%-accurate ground truth. This trains classical classifiers from labels; it does not fine-tune an LLM or transfer neural weights.

The 33 native-line features cover font size relative to document body text, font-size rank, bold/italic proportions, RGB color, normalized position/width/height, gaps, adjacent-line style/block indicators, repeated-text count, log character/word counts, uppercase/digit fractions, numeric-prefix depth, number-only lines, dot leaders, sentence endings and a generic multilingual caption-prefix indicator. Body font size is the size accounting for the most characters. These are engineered features, including text-pattern indicators; this is not a rule-free model.

sections.title: What was actually tuned
paragraphs: Two estimator families were compared using validation exact-level LINE F1: logistic regression 47.6%, Extra Trees 69.1%. Tree parameters and logistic C were fixed, not searched. Validation contains 21 heading groups across four reports; the separate v1 test contains 27 groups across four reports.

The v1 test scored 82.0% exact-level line F1 and 22/27 complete heading groups at the right level. This differs from the v2 group-F1 metric. The v1 training set was expanded with additional reviewed training pages before the reported selection/test; it is smaller than the later 887-group v2 set.

sections.title: Export and measured scope

Runtime inference uses NumPy and float32 tree traversal; it needs no LLM or scikit-learn model server. Full native text is retained. Parent IDs are derived from the predicted level stack, not separately learned or evaluated.

The main comparison parses all four historical PDFs (523 pages) on an Apple M4 Pro with 48 GB memory, but scores only 77 headings on 32 audited pages. Its fuzzy title matching plus exact level is different from the supervised exact group-and-level F1. Main-table scores are historical diagnostics, not the fresh supervised split. sections.title: What each model learns
paragraphs: The 33 native-line features cover font size relative to document body text, font-size rank, bold/italic proportions, RGB color, normalized position/width/height, gaps, adjacent-line style/block indicators, repeated-text count, log character/word counts, uppercase/digit fractions, numeric-prefix depth, number-only lines, dot leaders, sentence endings and a generic multilingual caption-prefix indicator. The context classifier uses 47 features: the 43 group features plus style_numbered_count, style_mean_depth, style_max_depth and toc_exact_title. TOC matching normalizes title text, strips its numeric prefix and dot leaders, and checks exact membership among dot-leader lines. This is a learned input feature, not a hard TOC level override.

The relationship classifier uses 142 features: two 47-feature groups, their differences and page delta. Its 867 training pairs are consecutive annotated headings. Target −1 means the next H number is smaller (shallower), 0 means equal and +1 means larger (deeper). It learns direction, not the number of levels skipped.

sections.title: Sequence decoding
paragraphs: First, body/heading argmax decides which predicted groups survive. Viterbi then maximizes the sum of log heading-class probabilities and weighted log relationship probabilities for transitions between retained groups. Transition class is sign(next H − previous H); probabilities are clipped below at 1e-12. Default relation weight is 1.0. This decoder is an algorithm, not a fourth trained model, and cannot recover a group already rejected as body.

sections.title: What calibration changes
paragraphs: Only the body column of a copy of the group-probability array is multiplied by body_weight before argmax. Surviving headings still use the original probabilities in Viterbi. This is decision weighting, not statistical probability calibration.

On the four validation reports, body weights 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 yield group-and-level F1 of 69.8%, 76.9% and 81.1%. All three relationship weights tie at each body weight, so the ordered grid retains relation_weight=1.0. There is no evidence from this grid that a relationship-weight change helped.

sections.title: Regression outcome and why this is not promoted
paragraphs: On the previously inspected 38-heading set, F1 rises from 85.7% to 94.7%: 36 groups remain correctly leveled, false groups fall from 8 to 1, and one genuine group is now missed. This is regression evidence, not a new independent test.
